title: Stable-channel mapping and safety rollback orchestration for model/runtime pairings
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
Teams continue to run into surprising incompatibilities when models and runtime versions diverge. Current routing rules are ad-hoc per-release and rely on manual edits to allowlists/fallbacks. That increases rollback complexity and makes safe tenant upgrades slow and error-prone.

Goal:
Introduce a channel-aware routing and rollback orchestration layer that: (1) understands model↔runtime compat semantics (semver + opt-in feature flags), (2) provides LTS/stable channels for runtime families, (3) enables declarative pinning of model versions to runtime channels, and (4) automates safe fallback and rollback behavior during rollouts and incidents.

Proposal (high-level):
- Compatibility model: maintain a canonical compat matrix where entries are semver ranges for runtime that each model version supports plus a small set of runtime feature gates (e.g., kv-cache-v2, attention-kernel-v3). Matrix is derived from onboarding test results and developer annotations.
- Channels: expose runtime channels (stable-LTS, stable, canary) that map to specific semver ranges and patch policies. Customers and internal workflows can pin to a channel string (e.g., "runtime:stable-LTS-2025-11").
- Routing layer: implement a channel-aware router that resolves a requested model + tenant to a concrete runtime instance based on (a) explicit tenant pin, (b) model's compat range, (c) channel defaults, and (d) live health/latency/capacity signals.
- Fallback policies: declarative policy objects that specify fallback precedence (e.g., prefer model-variant fallback first, then runtime-compatible downgrade to prev-patch, finally region fallback). Each policy has a TTL and circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid thrashing.
- Rollout orchestration: wired into release-infra—supports canary percentages, staged traffic groups, automated gating checks (latency, error-rate, token-cost per response, quality regressions measured by synthetic evals). Failed gates trigger automated rollback to last-known-good channel for affected tenants.
- Tooling: CLI to propose channel mappings, dry-run diff of routing decisions, and generator that emits migration playbooks (tenant lists, rollback steps).

Acceptance criteria:
- Compatibility matrix stored in Git as machine-readable YAML and surfaced in Console.
- Router resolves model->runtime decision in <10ms P95 for control-plane lookups.
- Rollout orchestration can do a staged rollout (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with automated gates; failing gate stops progression and triggers documented rollback steps.
- Integration tests: synthetic suite that exercises at least 20 model/runtime pairings across channels and asserts zero crashes and bounded latency regressions (<20% QPS impact in canary).

Backward compatibility considerations:
- Default behavior for tenants without explicit pins remains unchanged (router uses current global defaults).
- New channel strings are opt-in; existing routing rules are source-of-truth until we flip a migration flag per-team.

Monitoring & alerting:
- New dashboard "compatibility-matrix" showing per-model supported runtimes and onboarding status.
- Rollout gate metrics: canary_error_rate, canary_latency_pct_p95, canary_quality_delta.
- Pager rules: if rollback automation triggers for >3 tenants in 10 minutes, escalate to on-call release-engineering.

Migration plan (tenants):
1) Export current pin map; run compatibility scan against matrix and mark conflicts.
2) Notify affected customers via account teams for manual resolution where model/runtime feature gates mismatch.
3) For safe tenants, schedule staged migration using rollout orchestration with monitoring and auto-rollback.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Where to store compat matrix: Git + small backing kv store vs database with UI. Trade-off: Git gives auditability + PR workflow; DB allows quicker writes for live fixes. Proposed hybrid: Git for authoritative matrix, DB cache for router performance and fast edits.
- Fallback semantics: conservative vs permissive. Conservative avoids surprising correctness regressions but increases unavailability in edge cases. We default conservative for now (prefer model-variant fallback and reject cross-feature downgrade).

Next steps / Milestones:
- [Week 1] RFC sign-off and matrix schema agreed (owner: Diego).
- [Week 2] Prototype router lookup and DB cache; skeleton rollout orchestrator implementation.
- [Week 3] Integrate gating metrics and simple rollback action.
- [Week 4] End-to-end test run + internal dogfooding + create Console surface.

Owners and reviewers:
- Owner: Diego Morales (release infra)
- Reviewers: Priya Nair (runtime), Marcus Li (platform reliability), Sofia Karim (console)

Dependencies and cross-team work:
- Runtime team: ensure runtime emits feature-gate metadata (ENG-21904).
- Console: UI surface for channel pinning and matrix view.
- Evals team: maintain small synthetic prompt set used by rollout gates.
